target: scripts/build_lot_search_index.py - keyset cursor on the compute-phase batch SELECT
findings_summary: Measured live: small LGAs compute at ~490 lots/s (24,903 done in 51s) WITH all indexes present, so index maintenance is NOT the bottleneck. A 102,934-lot LGA runs at ~23 lots/s and DEGRADES (10k per 7min, then 10k per 10min) because the batch SELECT filters on lga_name plus computed_at IS NULL, ordered by lotidstring with a LIMIT and no cursor, so every batch re-scans the rows it already stamped. Fix: add a lotidstring > cursor bound. Correctness: every selected row is stamped computed_at=NOW() in the same execute_values UPDATE, so all rows below the cursor are stamped and the extra predicate is a seek hint rather than a semantic change; a batch returning fewer than LIMIT rows still means the LGA is exhausted. It is also strictly SAFER than the current code: a row that somehow fails to be stamped loops forever today, whereas the cursor advances past it.
